source.section: PDF pages 9-10, Line 29 (59 1/2 before January 1, 2025; Married taxpayers: each spouse's own income, no unused part of the spouse's exclusion); Form IT-201 line 29; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Married filing jointly. Person 0, 66: IRA 30,000 and private pension 10,000. Person 1, 57 (reaches 59 1/2 in 2027): IRA 25,000 and wages 60,000. Each person's age and income count separately. Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 125,000.00. Federal taxable income = 125,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 1,600 age-65 addition = 91,900.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 29 exclusion, person 0 (66): IRA 30,000 + private pension 10,000 = 40,000, limited to 20,000 20,000.00. Subtraction: line 29 exclusion, person 1 (57, under 59 1/2 all year): 0; the IRA 25,000 stays taxable and person 0's limit cannot cover it 0.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 20,000.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 125,000.00 - 20,000.00 = 105,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (married joint, PDF page 11 table) 16,050.00; line 35 = 105,000.00 - 16,050.00 = 88,950.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 88,950.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, married joint) on 88,950.00: 17,150.00 x 4% = 686.00; 6,450.00 x 4.5% = 290.25; 4,300.00 x 5.25% = 225.75; 61,050.00 x 5.5% = 3,357.75; schedule tax = 4,559.75. NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 4,559.75. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 4,559.75.
